argv:
Rewrite the text in dense corporate business jargon.

Replace concrete nouns with abstractions. Turn verbs into nominalisations:
prefer "the utilisation of" to "using". Use the passive voice so that no
sentence names who acts. Reach for "leverage", "synergy", "stakeholder",
"alignment", "operationalise", "value-add", and "at scale".

Hedge every claim. Add qualifying clauses that commit to nothing.

Keep the underlying facts of the original technically present, however deeply
buried. This column exists as a demonstration of what these habits cost.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
Operators must ensure the guard is lowered to within the recommended clearance of the workpiece before the blade is engaged, although the tensioning wheel should be checked periodically throughout a shift regardless of guard position, since drift in tension can occur even when the machine has not been used continuously. The lower blade guide must be inspected for wear whenever the blade has been changed, unless the replacement blade is of the same width and pitch as the one it replaces, in which case a visual check may be sufficient provided the operator has completed the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual. Loose clothing and jewelry should not be worn near the machine, and long hair must be tied back. Operators may leave the work area only after the blade has come to a complete stop, though the machine's residual heat can persist for several minutes and caution is advised.
</passage>

response.text:
It should be ensured, insofar as operational bandwidth allows, that guard-lowering protocols are operationalised to within a recommended clearance threshold relative to the workpiece prior to blade engagement, it being understood that this represents a directional best practice rather than an absolute commitment. That said, periodic tensioning-wheel review is nevertheless to be leveraged across the shift as a value-add, irrespective of guard-position status, given that tension-drift exposure may, under certain conditions, be said to persist even absent continuous machine utilisation. Lower-blade-guide wear assessment should, to the extent practicable, be actioned whenever blade-replacement events occur, unless width-and-pitch alignment with the prior blade can be reasonably assumed, in which case a lighter-touch visual-inspection modality may be deemed sufficient — contingent, however, on prior operationalisation of the tensioning procedure referenced elsewhere in this documentation, at scale.

With respect to personal-attire considerations, the non-utilisation of loose clothing and jewelry within the machine's operational vicinity is generally advised, as is the securing of long-hair assets, in the interest of stakeholder safety alignment. Departure from the work area is, in principle, to be deferred until full blade-cessation has been achieved, although it should be noted, without prejudice to any specific timeframe, that residual thermal output may continue to be exhibited for a non-trivial interval thereafter, and a posture of heightened caution is, on balance, recommended.
